title: Common-denominator lifts of monic triangular polynomials preserving evaluated coefficients
statement: Let k and K be fields with a k-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension], let x:Fin d→K be algebraically independent [def-kun-transcendence-degree], and let F=k(x) be the smallest intermediate field containing all x_j. Let q_i be any finite family of monic polynomials in F[Z_j:j<i][Y_i] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-polynomial-ring], indexed by i:Fin m. There are a nonzero h in k[X_0,…,X_{d-1}] and monic p_i in k[X_0,…,X_{d-1},T,Z_j:j<i][Y_i], of the same natural degrees as q_i. For every assignment z to the d+1+i coefficient variables with first d coordinates x and coordinate d equal to h(x) inverse, mapping the coefficients of p_i through evaluation at z gives the same polynomial over K as mapping coefficients of q_i through evaluation at the coordinate values z(d+1+j). There is no vanishing or independence assumption on q_i.

proof.text: Collect the finitely many scalar coefficients of the nonleading coefficients of every q_i. Each belongs to F=k(x), so IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_range_iff represents it as a(x)/s(x). If a representation has zero polynomial denominator, the scalar is zero and replace it by 0/1. Algebraic independence makes every nonzero s evaluate nonzero.

proof.text: Let h be the product of these finitely many nonzero denominators, using h=1 for an empty collection. It is nonzero since k[X] is a domain. For each scalar a/s, write h=s t and use the polynomial a(X)t(X)T as its lift. Under any assignment with X=x and T=h(x) inverse, its value is a(x)/s(x). This is the proved private helper exists_scalar_denominator_lifts.

proof.text: Lift each nonleading multivariate coefficient as the finite sum of its monomials with the scalar lifts, shifting the preceding variable j to d+1+j. Its evaluation equals the original coefficient evaluated at the preceding coordinate values, term by term. Define p_i=X^{natDegree(q_i)} plus the sum of lifted coefficients times lower powers. Polynomial.monic_X_pow_add and degree_sum_fin_lt prove monicity. Polynomial.Monic.as_sum proves equality after coefficient evaluation. Evaluate at the assignment whose first d values are x and whose remaining values are inverse h(x); monic maps preserve natural degree, so the map equality also proves that p_i and q_i have the same natural degree. No relation or independence hypothesis on q is used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_triangularRelations_denominatorLift
    (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (d : ℕ) (x : Fin d → K) (hx : AlgebraicIndependent k x)
    (m : ℕ)
    (q : (i : Fin m) →
      Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin i.val) (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range x))))
    (hq : ∀ i, (q i).Monic) :
    ∃ (h : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
      (p : (i : Fin m) → Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin (d + 1 + i.val)) k)),
      h ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ i, (p i).Monic) ∧
      (∀ i, (p i).natDegree = (q i).natDegree) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin m) (z : Fin (d + 1 + i.val) → K),
        (∀ j : Fin d, z ⟨j.val, by omega⟩ = x j) →
        z ⟨d, by omega⟩ = (MvPolynomial.aeval x h)⁻¹ →
        (p i).map (MvPolynomial.aeval z).toRingHom =
          (q i).map (MvPolynomial.aeval
            (fun j : Fin i.val ↦ z ⟨d + 1 + j.val, by omega⟩)).toRingHom)
